name: HumanEval / HumanEval+
rationale_for_inclusion: Most-cited code benchmark globally; acknowledged as saturated but serves as a controlled baseline for C02; HumanEval+ adds 80x more test cases reducing false positives. Appears in GPT-4 / Claude 3 / Gemini 1.0 / Llama 3 reports.

name: MBPP / MBPP+ (EvalPlus)
rationale_for_inclusion: Broader Python coverage (~974 problems) than HumanEval; EvalPlus version increases test rigour. Cited in GPT-4 / Claude 3 / Gemini 1.0 / Llama 3 technical reports. Complements HumanEval's narrower function-completion scope.

name: SWE-bench Verified
rationale_for_inclusion: De-facto agentic-coding standard in 2025; 500 human-verified real GitHub issues. Exposes the gap between isolated function generation (HumanEval) and real-world software engineering. Cited in Claude 4 / Gemini 2.5 / Llama 4 reports.

name: LiveCodeBench
rationale_for_inclusion: Addresses contamination through monthly problem refresh from competitive programming sites. Cited in Claude 4 / Gemini 2.5 / Llama 4 reports. Provides a temporally-stable signal not confounded by data leakage.

name: BigCodeBench (Hard)
rationale_for_inclusion: 148 hard tasks requiring real library and tool integration; richer and more realistic than HumanEval. Cited in Claude 4 / Gemini 2.5 reports. Measures software engineering depth rather than algorithmic puzzle-solving.

name: IFEval
rationale_for_inclusion: Only C01 benchmark with cross-lab consensus (Claude 4 / Gemini 2.5 / Llama 4 / OLLMv2). Surfaces the C01 proxy problem: it measures verifiable constraint-following on short prompts rather than creative or long-form writing quality. Essential as a baseline to demonstrate the coverage gap.

name: WritingBench
rationale_for_inclusion: 1239 queries across 6 writing domains and 100 subdomains; query-dependent critic model avoids one-size rubric problems. NeurIPS 2025. Directly addresses the C01 gap and covers creative / persuasive / informative / technical writing. No frontier technical report cites it — illustrating the gap itself.

name: EQ-Bench Creative Writing v3 + Longform Writing
rationale_for_inclusion: LLM-judged with Elo + rubric; captures style / voice / humour / spatial awareness / character voice dimensions absent from IFEval. Has an active public leaderboard (eqbench.com). Provides a live community-maintained signal for open-ended writing quality.

name: HelloBench / LongBench-Write
rationale_for_inclusion: Closes the single-sentence-prompt limitation: HelloBench uses task-specific evaluation dimensions for long-form generation; LongBench-Write provides six fixed dimensions across document types. Together they cover C01 at the document length actually used in real workflows.

name: MathDial
rationale_for_inclusion: Foundational tutoring-dialogue dataset: 2900 student–tutor dialogues grounded in GSM8K problems. EMNLP 2023. Grounds subsequent C04 benchmarks and establishes the distinction between solving a maths problem and teaching a student to solve it.

name: MRBench
rationale_for_inclusion: 192 tutoring dialogues × 7 LLM tutors × 8 explicit pedagogical dimensions; uses Desired Annotation Match Rate metric (NAACL 2025). The most multi-dimensional C04 benchmark available; operationalises pedagogy across scaffolding / error correction / encouragement.

name: MathTutorBench
rationale_for_inclusion: 7 pedagogical tasks including scaffolding / mistake localisation / pedagogy-following; first C04 benchmark with a pedagogy reward model and a public leaderboard. 2025. Directly replicable and extensible; addresses the key finding that stronger solvers are often worse tutors.

name: MMLU / MMLU-Pro
rationale_for_inclusion: Universal factual-knowledge baseline (MMLU) and its contamination-resistant 2024 update (MMLU-Pro). Combined they appear in every major frontier model report across all labs. MMLU-Pro's harder reasoning-focused items reduce ceiling effects that plague MMLU.

name: GPQA Diamond
rationale_for_inclusion: Graduate-level science MCQ validated by domain experts; gated to resist contamination. Present in every major 2025 frontier release table (Claude 4 / Gemini 2.5 / Llama 4). Has replaced MMLU as the frontier difficulty benchmark for factual knowledge.

name: TriviaQA / Natural Questions
rationale_for_inclusion: Classic open-domain retrieval QA benchmarks still cited by Llama 3 and Gemini 1.5; represent real-world information-seeking queries at paragraph and document length. Provide lower-difficulty anchor points in the C03 coverage spectrum.

name: SimpleQA / FACTS Grounding
rationale_for_inclusion: Directly measure hallucination: SimpleQA (OpenAI) uses 4326 unambiguous short-answer questions; FACTS Grounding (Google) uses 860 grounding tasks against provided context. Both cited in Claude 4 / Gemini 2.0 reports. Fill a hallucination-measurement gap in C03.

name: CriticBench (Tsinghua)
rationale_for_inclusion: Most comprehensive C05 benchmark: 15 datasets across math / commonsense / symbolic / code / algorithmic critique-and-correct. ACL 2024 Findings. Only critique benchmark with cross-reasoning-domain coverage. Not cited in any frontier technical report — illustrating the C05 gap.

name: Auto-J + Shepherd + MetaCritique (grouped)
rationale_for_inclusion: Complement CriticBench by covering open-ended critique tasks (essay feedback / code review / general instruction following). Critique-tuned model evaluations with human-annotated references. Together with CriticBench they form minimum viable C05 coverage. None appears in any frontier model report.
